name: Identification schemes, granularity and physical data carriers (cross-family)
scope_note: Covers how DPP implementations identify the product (model, batch, item), the economic operators and the facilities, how they put that identifier on a physical carrier (QR code, GS1 DataMatrix, NFC NDEF, NFC secure dynamic messages, UHF RFID EPC, digital watermark, direct part marking), how the carrier identifier is turned into a passport (resolution), and what a black-box tester can verify from sample artifacts. Schemes: GS1 keys and Digital Link URIs, EPC URIs and binary encodings, AAS asset identifiers, Catena-X BPN and specific asset ids, W3C DIDs (did:web), UUID URNs, UNTP URN and IDR URL patterns, DOI, LEI, EORI, GLN. Leaves out: passport payload data models (see other method files), access-control and credential formats beyond carrier binding, and the content of every EN, ISO, IEC and DIN document (bibliographic metadata only, rule 5). NFC Forum specifications are licence-gated and were not read; NDEF layout is described only from the open-source ndeflib code.
summary: Every DPP family rests on the same physical-to-digital chain: an identifier is issued (by an issuing agency or self-issued), encoded on a data carrier that is physically present on the product, packaging or documents (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(a)-(b)), and resolved to the passport. EU law fixes the roles (unique product, operator and facility identifiers, Art. 2(30), (31), (33)) and the granularity choice (model, batch or item, Art. 9(2)(d) and Art. 10(1)(f)), but names no scheme beyond the ISO/IEC 15459 series and the GTIN in Annex III; the scheme comes from the implementation family. The GS1 family encodes granularity in the URI path of a GS1 Digital Link: /01/{GTIN-14} is model level, adding /10/{lot} is batch level and /21/{serial} is item level, with qualifiers in the fixed order 22, 10, 21, and a resolver walks up from item to product-class links. The same GS1 keys appear on UHF RFID as EPC binary strings (SGTIN-96 header 0x30, or the newer SGTIN+, DSGTIN+ and TDS 2.3 '++' schemes that also carry the brand domain), on GS1 DataMatrix and GS1 QR Code as FNC1-prefixed element strings, and on NFC tags as an NDEF URI record. The AAS family identifies the asset through AssetInformation.globalAssetId and specificAssetIds, with AssetKind Type, Instance and, new in IDTA-01001 version 3.2, Batch; lookup goes through the AAS Discovery service, and IDTA 02099-1 adds explicit uniqueProductIdentifier, granularity, economicOperatorId and facilityId elements. Catena-X identifies companies, sites and addresses with 16-character BPNL, BPNS and BPNA numbers from one licensed issuing organisation and finds a twin by manufacturerPartId and partInstanceId through BPN discovery, EDC discovery and a decentral digital twin registry. The SSI family uses self-issued did:web identifiers that map to an HTTPS did.json, and UNTP proposes URN, IDR URL, DID and UUID patterns plus a resolver that returns RFC 9264 linksets with the IANA-registered 'dpp' link relation. Carrier-to-passport binding is digital only: signed payloads or secure dynamic NFC messages (AES-CMAC over UID and a tap counter on NXP NTAG 424 DNA) can show that a tag produced a fresh message, but no digital check proves that the tag is on the genuine product. The EU registry (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8) checks granularity, links item passports to batch and model identifiers, and returns a registration identifier. A conformance engine can test most of this from sample artifacts: decode a QR or DataMatrix image, parse an NDEF dump, decode an EPC hex string, check identifier syntax and check digits, compare the carrier identifier, the passport identifier, the registry record and the declared granularity, and probe a resolver on loopback for status codes and linksets, but today it covers only QR decoding, one GS1 Digital Link form (/01/{GTIN}/21/{serial}) and exact-text comparison, so batch and model carriers, other symbologies, NFC and RFID samples, operator identifiers and resolver conformance need new capabilities.

maturity.spec_status: Mixed. EU law is in force (ESPR, Batteries Regulation, registry act); identifier life-cycle rules under ESPR Art. 12(4) are not yet adopted (not located on 2026-10-13, not re-checked). Harmonised standards on unique identifiers and data carriers (EN 18219:2026, EN 18220:2026) are cited in the Annex of Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736; their content is protected and not used. GS1 specifications are ratified and current (Digital Link 1.7.0, Resolver 1.2.1, TDS 2.3, Gen2 3.0.1). IDTA AAS 3.2 is released; IDTA 02099-1 1.0.1 is published. W3C DID 1.1 is a Candidate Recommendation Snapshot; did:web is a W3C CCG draft without a shown status. UNTP Identity Resolver is pre-1.0 (GitLab main uses v0.8.0 artefact paths). NFC secure dynamic messaging is vendor-specific (NXP application note).

maturity.adoption_evidence: GS1 keys and EPC Gen2 RFID are in wide commercial use (not quantified here). GS1 Digital Link resolvers for DPP are reported in peer-reviewed prototypes: a GS1-conformant resolver with scanning over QR, NFC, RFID, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth deployed for supply chains and DPPs (Park et al. 2025, 10.1109/rfid-ta63091.2025.11265909) and a lifecycle-aware GS1 resolver with fallback when the manufacturer ceases (Howie et al. 2026, 10.1016/j.procs.2026.02.212). A GS1-based plastics DPP pilot traced 2192 frisbees from bottle caps (Rumetshofer et al. 2024, 10.3390/polym16101420). DIDs with QR and NFC carriers were compared in a construction prototype, where QR outperformed NFC in ease of use (Byers et al. 2025, 10.1108/ci-02-2025-0074). Catena-X ran a reference DPP app (Eclipse Tractus-X digital-product-pass, Apache-2.0, now archived) that reads a partInstanceId from a QR code. The open-source GS1 Resolver CE reached version 3.0.0. NFC-based battery passport and UHF RFID battery traceability demonstrators exist (10.1109/rfid-ta64374.2024.10965188; 10.1109/metroautomotive57488.2023.10219134). No independent figure on the share of DPP pilots per carrier was verified.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781: Art. 2(29) defines a data carrier as a linear barcode, 2D symbol or other device-readable AIDC medium; Art. 2(30) the unique product identifier as a unique string that also enables a web link to the DPP; Art. 2(31) the unique operator identifier; Art. 2(33) the unique facility identifier. Art. 9(2)(b)-(d) leaves the carrier, its layout and position, and the model, batch or item level to each delegated act. Art. 10(1)(a)-(c) requires a carrier physically present on product, packaging or documents, linked to a persistent unique product identifier, and compliance with the Annex III standards or equivalents until harmonised standards are cited; Art. 10(1)(f) ties the data to the chosen level. Art. 10(3) requires a free digital copy of the carrier or identifier for dealers and marketplaces within five working days. Art. 12(1)-(3) governs operator and facility identifiers, including requests on behalf of other actors; Art. 12(4)-(6) empowers delegated acts on issuing agencies and on self-created identifiers that must be reliable, verifiable and globally unique. Art. 13(1) makes the registry store at least the unique identifiers (and battery identifiers). Annex III points (b), (c), (g), (h), (i), (k) and its second paragraph name the identifier roles and the ISO/IEC 15459-1 to -6 editions (bibliographic only). Regulation (EU) 2023/1542: Art. 13(6)-(7) and Annex VI Part C require a visible, legible, indelible, high-contrast QR code readable by common readers; Art. 77(3) links the QR code to an operator-assigned unique identifier; Art. 77(7) gives a repurposed or remanufactured battery a new passport linked to the original; Art. 77(8) ends the passport after recycling; Art. 77(10) requires upload of the identifier to the ESPR registry. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8(1)-(10): registration at the level set by Union law, the most granular level where rules differ, item-level passports linked to batch and model identifiers, automated granularity checks, and a persistent registration identifier.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: GS1: GTIN is AI 01, format N2+N14 with a mod-10 check digit flag; batch/lot AI 10, serial AI 21 and CPV AI 22 are 1 to 20 characters from GS1 character set 82 (letters, digits and listed symbols); TPX AI 235 (1 to 28 characters) requires 01 and AI 21 excludes 235; GLN of a physical location AI 414 (N13 with check digit; qualifiers 254 and 7040); invoicing-party GLN AI 415 (qualifier 8020); party GLN AI 417; GIAI AI 8004 (1 to 30 characters, qualifier 7040); GRAI AI 8003 (N14 with check digit plus up to 16 serial characters); ITIP AI 8006 (qualifiers 22, 10, 21); GMN AI 8013 (1 to 25 characters with check characters); CPID AI 8010 with serial 8011. Granularity in GS1: model = GTIN (or GMN for a model number), batch = GTIN + AI 10, item = GTIN + AI 21 (SGTIN) or GIAI for an asset. GS1 Digital Link URI: https://{domain}[/{custom-prefix}...]/01/{GTIN-14}[/22/{cpv}][/10/{lot}][/21/{serial}][?{AI}={value}...]; GTIN-8/12/13 are zero-padded to 14 digits (mandatory since 1.4.0); reserved characters in values are percent-encoded (a slash becomes %2F); linkType and context are reserved query keys. Canonical form: https, host id.gs1.org, 14-digit GTIN, only AI keys in the query, keys sorted, no trailing slash. EPC pure-identity URI: urn:epc:id:sgtin:{CompanyPrefix}.{IndicatorAndItemRef}.{Serial}; tag URI urn:epc:tag:sgtin-96:{filter}.{CompanyPrefix}.{ItemRef}.{Serial}; the TDS 2.0+ '+' and 2.3 '++' schemes have no URN form and map to element strings and Digital Link URIs. AAS: Identifiable.id for the shell, AssetInformation.globalAssetId (Identifier, 0..1) and specificAssetIds (name, value, optional externalSubjectId as an external reference); Constraint AASd-131 needs one of them; 'globalAssetId' is a reserved specificAssetId name (AASd-116); a specific asset id is not necessarily globally unique; AssetKind values Type, Instance, Batch (added in 3.2 for DPP), Role, NotApplicable. IDTA 02099-1: digitalProductPassportId, uniqueProductIdentifier, granularity (Model, Batch, Item), economicOperatorId, facilityId (0..1). Catena-X: BPN is 16 characters, 'BPN' + type letter L, S or A + 10 entity characters + 2 check characters (upper-case letters and digits; check scheme named by Catena-X as ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 1271-36, bibliographic only); twins carry specificAssetIds manufacturerPartId and partInstanceId. W3C DID: did:{method}:{method-specific-id}, method name lower-case letters and digits, id segments of letters, digits, '.', '-', '_' and percent-encoded bytes separated by ':'; did:web uses a DNS name (not an IP address), port as %3A, path segments as ':'. UUID (RFC 9562): 128 bits as 8-4-4-4-12 hex, version nibble in octet 6, variant bits 10 in octet 8, URN form urn:uuid:{uuid}; v4 has 122 random bits, v7 starts with a 48-bit Unix millisecond timestamp. UNTP proposes urn:{ns}:{scheme}:{value}, urn:gtr:{dns-scheme}:{value} (IANA registration pending), IDR URLs https://{scheme-domain}/{path}, and the non-URN form uuid:{UUID}. LEI: 20 characters, LOU prefix (1-4), two reserved zeros (5-6), entity part (7-18), two check digits (19-20) per the LEI ROC page; non-reuse and one LEI per entity. EORI: two-letter issuing country code plus up to 15 alphanumeric characters unique in that country; one valid EORI per person; numbers do not expire. DOI: prefix starting '10.' and a registrant-chosen suffix separated by '/', case-insensitive for Basic Latin, never reassigned (secondary_only: search excerpts of the DOI Handbook).

L01_unique_identifiers.observable_black_box: From a carrier sample or passport document: the identifier string, its scheme (by prefix or pattern), its syntax, its check digit, its granularity (presence of AI 10 or 21, AssetKind, IDTA granularity), and whether the same string appears in the passport, the registry record and the resolver linkset. Global uniqueness and issuance authority cannot be proven from outside; only a collision within a sample set or a registry answer is observable.
L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: Law requires uniqueness, persistence, standard compliance and the granularity chosen per delegated act; it does not prescribe syntax, check digits, URL form or scheme. Schemes add syntax, check-digit and qualifier-order rules that are testable; ESPR Art. 12(5)(c) asks for verifiable identifiers but the delegated act is not located (as of 2026-10-13).

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: GS1 Data Carriers finding (1.0.2) groups carriers: Type A with defined GS1 syntax (EAN/UPC, ITF-14; GS1-128, GS1 DataMatrix, GS1 DataBar, GS1 QR Code, GS1 DotCode, GS1 Composite with element strings; QR Code and Data Matrix carrying a GS1 Digital Link URI; UHF and HF EPC/RFID with EPC binary); Type B candidates (NFC tag, Han Xin Code, digital watermark); Type C (for example Channel Code). GS1 content is signalled by FNC1 in GS1-128, GS1 QR Code and GS1 DataMatrix, by absence of FNC1 in GS1 DotCode, by the GS1 Digital Link regular expression in QR Code and Data Matrix that carry a URI, and by a toggle bit set to zero in EPC/RFID. NFC: an NDEF message with a well-known URI record (record type urn:nfc:wkt:U; payload byte 0 is a URI identifier code: 0x00 none, 0x03 'http://', 0x04 'https://', 0x1E 'urn:epc:id:', 0x1F 'urn:epc:tag:', 0x23 'urn:nfc:' in ndeflib's 36-entry table) followed by the UTF-8 rest of the IRI. NFC secure dynamic message (NXP NTAG 424 DNA SUN): on each unauthenticated read the tag mirrors ASCII hex into the NDEF URL, for example https://ntag.nxp.com/424?e={32 hex PICCData ciphertext}&c={16 hex truncated CMAC}; PICCData = PICCDataTag (1 byte; bit 7 UID mirroring, bit 6 counter mirroring, bits 3-0 UID length) || UID (7 bytes) || SDMReadCtr (3 bytes, LSB first) || padding, encrypted with AES-128 CBC and a zero IV under the SDM meta-read key; session keys are AES-CMAC over SV1 (prefix C33C 0001 0080) and SV2 (prefix 3CC3 0001 0080) with UID and counter; the MAC is truncated to 8 bytes by keeping the even-numbered bytes S14..S0. UHF RFID: EPC memory bank (bank 01) holds PC bits and the EPC; first 8 bits are the header (SGTIN-96 0x30, SSCC-96 0x31, SGLN-96 0x32, GRAI-96 0x33, GIAI-96 0x34, SGTIN-198 0x36, SGTIN+ 0xF7, DSGTIN+ 0xFB, DSGTIN++ 0xFC, SGTIN++ 0xFD; 0xE2 is permanently reserved for TID); SGTIN-96 = header 8 bits, filter 3 bits (0-7), partition 3 bits, company prefix plus indicator/item reference 44 bits (company prefix 20-40 bits for 6-12 digits), serial 38 bits as an integer 0 to 274,877,906,943 with no leading zeros, mapped to https://id.gs1.org/01/{gtin}/21/{serial}; the TID bank (bank 10) holds tag-maker identification and an untraceable indicator. Digital watermark: GS1 key repeated invisibly across packaging artwork, read by image, IR or UV capture; GS1 noted in 2021 that a means to indicate GS1 data was not standardised, payload is limited, verification differs from symbol grading, and some technologies need a licence. Direct part marking: Data Matrix marked on the part itself (laser, dot peen, casting inserts); readability on low-contrast polymer parts was 89.36 percent in one study (10.3390/s23031619). Battery passports: QR code mandatory (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 13(6)), printed or engraved visibly, legibly and indelibly (Art. 13(7)), with high contrast and a size readable by common QR readers (Annex VI Part C).

L02_data_carriers.observable_black_box: An image of the carrier (decodable payload, symbology, number of symbols; not print grade), an NDEF dump (record type, URI code, URI), a SUN URL sequence (ciphertext, MAC, counter progress if a key is supplied), an EPC hex string (header, filter, partition, decoded key). Physical presence, placement, durability, contrast and legibility need an inspector (manual step) or a print-quality verifier outside the engine.
L02_data_carriers.law_delta: ESPR leaves the carrier type to delegated acts and the Battery Regulation fixes a QR code; GS1 and vendor specifications add encoding rules, RFID and NFC options and anti-cloning features that law does not mention. NFC Forum and protected ISO/IEC symbology texts cannot serve as open oracles.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: GS1-Conformant Resolver 1.2.1: HTTPS with GET, HEAD and OPTIONS and CORS; without a linkType the resolver redirects to the single gs1:defaultLink (or a gs1:defaultLinkMulti variant chosen by Accept-Language or other headers); linkType={prefix:type} redirects to a matching link or returns 404 if none exists (changed from 1.1, which redirected to the default); linkType=linkset or Accept: application/linkset+json returns the RFC 9264 linkset without redirect (application/json should get the same; application/ld+json and text/html also supported); 300 Multiple Choices when the best match is ambiguous; basic validation including check-digit calculation precedes lookup and failures get 400 Bad Request; 404 for a syntactically valid but unknown entity; never 200 OK for an error; the whole query string is passed to the redirect target; a granular identifier inherits links from less granular levels and the resolver should synthesise one answer rather than redirect to the less granular URI; pattern-based delegation to another resolver exposes the target in Location and may add Link rel gs1:handledBy; compressed EPC binary strings are decompressed and the uncompressed URI is used; the resolver description file /.well-known/gs1resolver (RFC 8615) has required resolverRoot and supportedPrimaryKeys. The page names no redirect status code (no 301, 302, 307 or 308). UNTP Identity Resolver (GitLab main, read 2026-10-19): 307 for redirects, 400 for invalid queries, 404 when nothing matches at any level (a linkset may be included), 200 for linkset requests; /.well-known/resolver (or /.well-known/gs1resolver) declares the service; linkset queries need no authentication; DPP link relation is the IANA-registered token 'dpp' (IANA lists it with UNTP as reference), GS1 https://ref.gs1.org/voc/dpp treated as equivalent; older passport versions carry rel predecessor-version; linkType=all is only a deprecated alias of linkset. did:web: replace ':' with '/', decode %3A, build https://{domain}[/{path}]/did.json or https://{domain}/.well-known/did.json, HTTP GET over TLS, check that the document id equals the DID; DNS over HTTPS recommended; Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for browsers. AAS Discovery V3.2.0_SSP-001: POST /lookup/shellsByAssetLink with a JSON array of AssetLink {name 1-64 chars, value 1-2048 chars} (name 'globalAssetId' searches the global asset id) returns a PagedResult of AAS ids; GET /lookup/shells?assetIds={base64url(SpecificAssetId JSON)} is deprecated; /lookup/shells/{aasIdentifier} with a UTF-8 base64url-encoded id. Catena-X (Tractus-X DPP app): Discovery Finder gives BPN Discovery and EDC Discovery endpoints; BPN Discovery is queried with type manufacturerPartId; EDC Discovery is queried by BPN; the decentral digital twin registry is searched by specificAssetIds such as partInstanceId; data is then negotiated through the EDC connector. NFC SUN: the tap URL goes to the brand backend, which decrypts PICCData, recomputes the CMAC with the session MAC key and checks that the counter grew before redirecting to the passport.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Identifier persistence: ESPR Art. 10(1)(a) requires a persistent unique product identifier. LEI and BPN are never reassigned, even after the entity ends (LEI ROC page; CX-0010). DOI names are never changed once assigned (secondary_only). did:web deactivation is removal of did.json and there is no built-in history, so a did:web product identifier dies with the domain or file. UNTP warns that URL identifiers suffer link rot when domains change; Howie et al. 2026 add a fallback resolver dashboard for discontinued manufacturers. The passport of a battery ends after recycling (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(8)); registry data are deleted ten years after registration unless Union law says otherwise (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 10(3), from prior research 2026-10-13, not re-read).
L06_storage_archiving_persistence.observable_black_box: Only over time: repeated resolution of the same identifier (needs persistence.scheduled, interface_only). A single run can only observe that a resolver or did.json answers now.
L06_storage_archiving_persistence.law_delta: Law requires persistence for at least the expected product lifetime (ESPR Art. 9(2)(i), per prior research raw/espr.json of 2026-10-13, not re-read in this session) but does not say how identifiers survive a domain change; schemes differ widely.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Carriers and resolvers are public by design: UNTP requires linkset queries without authentication and enforces confidentiality at link targets. UNTP proposes UUIDs as hard-to-guess item identifiers acting as a shared secret for item data, while RFC 9562 says UUIDs must not be used as security capabilities and implementations should not assume they are hard to guess; this is a conflict a tester should flag. Catena-X marks partInstanceId specific asset ids as readable per policy (PUBLIC_READABLE) in the digital twin registry. NFC SUN mirrors data only in the unauthenticated state; its keys must be kept server-side (AN12196 recommends HSM storage of master keys).

specs.component: data-retrieval README, Specific Asset Id Type

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.observable_black_box: Whether a public resolver answer leaks restricted links or item data; whether item ids are sequential or guessable in a sample set; covered partly by access.restricted_fields on passport channels.
L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.law_delta: ESPR Art. 10(1)(g) (per prior research raw/espr.json of 2026-10-13, not re-read in this session) and delegated acts define access rights; identifiers and carriers themselves carry no access rule in law.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Digital binding options: (1) signed passport or link targets (GS1 link type jws; JWS or VC targets in UNTP with media types application/vc+jwt or application/vc+ld+json); (2) cryptographic NFC: NTAG 424 DNA SUN gives per-tap AES-CMAC over UID and counter (symmetric, so only the key holder verifies), research tags add ECDSA signatures (Plos et al. 2013, NIST P-192) or public-key challenge-response; (3) did:web proves control of a web file, not of the whole domain or the product. What stays unverifiable digitally: that the tag or label is attached to the genuine product; tag reapplication from a genuine to a counterfeit product (Alzahrani et al. 2016) and cloning of static QR, NDEF or EPC data. Research directions: copy-detection QR patterns (2LQR, 10.3390/electronics10030320), RF fingerprinting of NFC tags (10.1109/jiot.2025.3605841). The EU registry returns a registration identifier after automated checks (Art. 8(7)-(10)); that communication is not proof of compliance (ESPR Art. 13(5), per prior research raw/espr.json of 2026-10-13, not re-read in this session).

specs.component: SDMMAC, MACt truncation, session key derivation

variants: Asymmetric tag signature (research and some vendor chips)
L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.observable_black_box: Signature validity of a target (integrity.jws), SUN MAC validity and counter freshness given a test key, replay of an earlier SUN URL. Never: physical authenticity.
L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.law_delta: ESPR Art. 12(5)(c) asks for reliable and verifiable identifiers and carriers; no carrier-level cryptography is required by law.

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: ESPR Art. 13(1): the Commission registry stores at least the unique identifiers, plus the commodity code for products released for free circulation, and battery identifiers under Art. 77(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542; Art. 77(10) requires the battery operator to upload the identifier. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8: registration at model, batch or item level as Union law sets; the most granular level where rules differ; an item-level passport is linked to batch and model identifiers where they exist, a batch-level passport to the model identifier; automated checks of semantic conformity, data coherence, granularity, commodity code and back-up link; a unique persistent registration identifier is returned through the UI or API. Recital 14 says the operator issues the batch and model identifiers. The batteries FAQ (Q4.1) says the registration identifier need not appear in the customs declaration for battery passports; the EORI number (country code plus up to 15 characters) identifies economic operators in customs and can be checked through the Commission EORI validation service (live; not used).
variants: Third-party registration where Union law allows it
API or UI or bulk upload
L09_registry_and_customs.observable_black_box: In a mock registry: the record identifier equals the carrier and passport identifier; granularity links exist; the registration identifier is present. Official registry checks need registry.official (interface_only) and authorisation.
L09_registry_and_customs.law_delta: none for the core duty; the registry act adds granularity linking and automated checks that delegated acts alone do not state.

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: ESPR Art. 12(5)(d) foresees rules for creating, maintaining, updating and withdrawing identifiers and carriers. Batteries: a repurposed, remanufactured or re-used battery gets a new passport linked to the original passport(s) and responsibility moves to the new operator (Art. 77(7); FAQ Q9.1, Q9.5); the FAQ does not say whether a new identifier is issued. AAS allows a shell without globalAssetId in the first life-cycle phase, with only internal specific asset ids, but requires it once shared. UNTP requires version metadata in links and a default pointing to the latest version; older versions carry predecessor-version. GS1 resolver 1.2.1 returns 404 for an unavailable link type instead of falling back to the default. did:web updates edit the same did.json without history.
variants: New identifier and new passport linked to predecessor (repurposing)
Identifier withdrawal at end of life
L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.observable_black_box: Successor and predecessor links in passports or linksets; whether the default link points to the newest version; persistence.versions for version history.
L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.law_delta: Battery law fixes the successor-link rule; ESPR leaves identifier updates to the pending Art. 12(4) delegated act.

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Issuing models: (a) issuing agency with a registered agency code (ISO/IEC 15459 registration, bibliographic only), for example GS1, where an EPC may only be commissioned by the licensee of the GS1 Company Prefix or its delegate (TDS 2.3); (b) agency networks for parties: LEI issued by Local Operating Units under the LEI ROC, EORI by Member State customs, BPN by one issuing organisation licensed by Catena-X e.V. and only for a matching golden record with a legal identifier such as VAT; (c) self-issued: HTTPS URLs and did:web on the operator domain, UUIDs (UNTP requirement 12 supports self-issued identifiers if equally discoverable, resolvable and verifiable). ESPR Art. 12(2)-(3): the operator creating or updating the DPP requests missing operator or facility identifiers on behalf of the relevant actor after checking none exists; Art. 12(4)(a)-(b) and 12(5)-(6): delegated acts on becoming an issuing agency and on self-created identifiers, technology-neutral and interoperable. The batteries FAQ Q5.2 says operators may create identifiers locally using an option in the relevant standards or use a commercial service. Resolver domain sovereignty: the domain owner controls the URL space and clients must not infer a resolver from a URL pattern (UNTP requirement 14; GS1 Digital Link 1.7.0 says applications must not assume a resolver).

L11_roles_and_governance.law_delta: The ESPR Art. 12(4) delegated act on issuing agencies and self-issuance was not located (2026-10-13, not re-checked); schemes run their own governance.

end_to_end_flows.name: Consumer scan of an item-level GS1 Digital Link QR code
steps: 1. The camera decodes the QR code to https://brand.example/01/09520123456788/21/ABC123.
2. The phone sends GET without linkType.
3. The resolver validates the AI syntax and the GTIN check digit (400 on failure).
4. It finds item links or walks up to GTIN-level links and redirects to the default link or a gs1:dpp link.
5. The passport host returns the passport (HTML or JSON) for the public access tier.

end_to_end_flows.name: Machine retrieval of a linkset
steps: 1. Software decodes the carrier and builds the Digital Link URI.
2. It sends GET with linkType=linkset or Accept: application/linkset+json.
3. The resolver returns 200 with an RFC 9264 linkset and no redirect.
4. Software selects the link with relation dpp (or gs1:dpp) and the newest version, then fetches it.

end_to_end_flows.name: Battery passport via QR code and registry
steps: 1. The operator assigns a unique identifier to the battery and builds the passport (Art. 77(3)).
2. It prints or engraves the QR code that links to the identifier (Art. 13(6)-(7)).
3. It uploads the identifier to the registry (Art. 77(10)); the registry checks granularity and returns a registration identifier (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8).
4. A reader scans the QR code and reaches the passport.
5. After repurposing, a new passport linked to the original is created (Art. 77(7)).

end_to_end_flows.name: AAS-based lookup from a carrier
steps: 1. The carrier yields a URL or identifier equal to the globalAssetId.
2. The app sends POST /lookup/shellsByAssetLink with [{name: globalAssetId, value: <id>}].
3. Discovery returns AAS ids; the app base64url-encodes one and looks up its descriptor in the registry.
4. The app reads the DPP submodels (for example IDTA 02099-1 metadata with granularity) from the repository endpoint.

end_to_end_flows.name: Catena-X dataspace retrieval
steps: 1. A QR code (or manual entry) gives a partInstanceId; the app also knows the manufacturerPartId.
2. Discovery Finder returns BPN Discovery and EDC Discovery endpoints.
3. BPN Discovery maps the manufacturerPartId to the manufacturer BPNL.
4. EDC Discovery returns the provider connector for that BPN.
5. The app negotiates access and searches the twin registry by specificAssetIds partInstanceId.
6. The passport submodel is fetched through the connector.

end_to_end_flows.name: did:web product identifier (UNTP pattern)
steps: 1. The carrier or credential holds did:web:sample-company.example:products:123456789.
2. Software maps it to https://sample-company.example/products/123456789/did.json.
3. It fetches the document over TLS and checks that its id equals the DID.
4. It selects the service whose type matches the wanted link type (for example a DPP) and fetches the credential.

end_to_end_flows.name: NFC secure dynamic message tap
steps: 1. The phone reads the NDEF URI; the tag has mirrored encrypted PICCData (e) and a truncated CMAC (c).
2. The phone opens the URL at the brand backend.
3. The backend decrypts PICCData with the meta-read key, derives the session MAC key from UID and counter, and recomputes the CMAC.
4. It accepts only if the MAC matches and the counter is higher than the last seen value.
5. It redirects to the passport, optionally marking the scan as authenticated tag presence.

end_to_end_flows.name: UHF RFID EPC read in logistics
steps: 1. The reader inventories tags and reads the EPC bank.
2. Software reads the header (0x30 for SGTIN-96), filter and partition, then the company prefix, item reference and serial.
3. It rebuilds the GTIN-14 with its check digit and forms https://id.gs1.org/01/{gtin}/21/{serial} (or a brand-domain URI for '++' schemes).
4. It resolves the URI as in the GS1 flow.

end_to_end_flows.name: Conformance engine sample-artifact test (target design)
steps: 1. The ICS declares the identifier scheme and granularity; the IXIT names carrier samples (image, NDEF dump, EPC hex, SUN URLs).
2. carrier.* checks decode each sample offline.
3. identifier.parse checks syntax and check digits per scheme.
4. identifier.resolve and identifier.consistency fetch from the SUT or a loopback mock and compare carrier, passport, item document and (mock) registry identifiers and granularity.
5. Physical presence and print quality go to manual.review.

failure_modes.fault: Wrong GTIN check digit in the Digital Link URI (typo or bad generator).
failure_modes.detectable_by: identifier.parse recomputes the mod-10 digit; a conformant resolver must answer 400.

failure_modes.fault: GTIN-13 or GTIN-12 not padded to 14 digits in the URI path.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Syntax check against Digital Link 1.4.0+ rules; exact comparison with a padded passport id fails.

failure_modes.fault: Qualifiers in the wrong order (/21/ before /10/) or AI 21 combined with AI 235.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Full Digital Link grammar and AI excludes list.

failure_modes.fault: Serial with an unencoded '/', '#' or '?', or longer than 20 characters.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Percent-encoding and length checks; the URI path splits wrongly.

failure_modes.fault: Valid GS1 serial with characters outside the engine's current set (for example '!' or a percent-encoded value) rejected by the tester.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Tester-side false negative: compare identifier.parse results with GS1 Barcode Syntax Tests vectors.

failure_modes.fault: The same serial printed on two items (duplicate identifier).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Collision across samples or registry records in one campaign; global uniqueness is not provable.

failure_modes.fault: Carrier and passport identifiers differ (http versus https, brand domain versus id.gs1.org, trailing slash, different serial).
failure_modes.detectable_by: identifier.consistency exact comparison; a canonical-equivalence mode would separate cosmetic from real mismatches.

failure_modes.fault: A batch-level carrier (GTIN plus lot) on a product whose passport is declared item-level.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Granularity comparison between carrier qualifiers and the passport granularity field.

failure_modes.fault: Operator identifier with a malformed GLN check digit, a 19-character LEI or an EORI without a country code.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Scheme-specific syntax checks of operator and facility fields.

failure_modes.fault: QR code too small, low contrast, missing quiet zone or damaged so phones cannot read it.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Decode failure on the sample image; grading needs an external verifier or manual.review.

failure_modes.fault: Two QR symbols on the label (for example a marketing code beside the DPP code) and the reader picks the wrong one.
failure_modes.detectable_by: carrier.qr_decode symbol count and payload comparison.

failure_modes.fault: NDEF URI record encodes http:// (code 0x03) while the passport id uses https://, or the URI is inside a Smart Poster record a simple reader skips.
failure_modes.detectable_by: NDEF dump parsing and identifier comparison.

failure_modes.fault: SGTIN-96 cannot hold an alphanumeric or leading-zero serial, so the RFID EPC and the QR serial differ.
failure_modes.detectable_by: EPC decode and comparison with the Digital Link serial.

failure_modes.fault: Wrong partition value (company prefix length) or filter value in the EPC, giving a different GTIN.
failure_modes.detectable_by: EPC decode, GTIN check digit and comparison with the passport.

failure_modes.fault: Watermark or GS1 DataMatrix carries only a GTIN (model level) while the product needs an item passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Granularity check on the decoded payload.

failure_modes.fault: Unresolvable URL: expired domain, DNS failure, TLS error or 404 for a printed identifier.
failure_modes.detectable_by: identifier.resolve reports unresolved or unreachable; repeated runs show persistence failures.

failure_modes.fault: Resolver answers 200 with an HTML error page for unknown or invalid identifiers.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Probe with an unknown and a bad-check-digit identifier; the resolver standard forbids 200 for errors.

failure_modes.fault: Resolver ignores linkType=linkset and redirects, or returns the linkset with a wrong media type.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Status code and Content-Type check against the resolver standard.

failure_modes.fault: did:web document id does not equal the DID, or did.json sits at the wrong path.
failure_modes.detectable_by: did:web mapping and id comparison on loopback.

failure_modes.fault: AAS shell without globalAssetId, or a specific asset id named 'globalAssetId' with a different value, or assetKind Type used for an item passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: AASd-131 and AASd-116 checks and assetKind versus granularity comparison.

failure_modes.detectable_by: Pattern analysis over a sample set; access.restricted_fields on target channels.

open_questions: Has the ESPR Art. 12(4) delegated act on issuing agencies and self-created identifiers been published or drafted since 2026-10-13? Not re-searched in this session.
Which granularity do the first ESPR product delegated acts set, and which data carrier types do they allow? Needed as ICS values for identifier.granularity.
Which open oracle can the engine use for LEI and BPN check characters, given that ISO/IEC 7064 is protected? Options: structural check only, or an owner-approved library (python-stdnum, LGPL-2.1).
Does the zxing-cpp Python result expose the symbology identifier (needed to recognise FNC1 and GS1 mode in DataMatrix and QR)? Not verified.
What is the GS1 check-character algorithm for GMN (AI 8013)? It sits in the GS1 General Specifications, which could not be fetched (file above 10 MB).
Does the GS1 resolver description file have a published JSON schema URL that can be pinned? The standard says it must validate against one; the URL was not captured.
May the AN12196 worked-example keys and values be redistributed as test vectors? Vendor copyright; self-generated TEST-ONLY vectors avoid the question.
Should the engine follow GS1 (no redirect code named) or UNTP (307) when judging redirect status codes? A conformance profile must pick per declared method.
Does a repurposed battery get a new unique identifier or keep the old one with a new passport? Art. 77(7) and FAQ Q9.5 require a new linked passport but are silent on the identifier.
Does the AAS 3.2 Batch asset kind become the expected encoding for batch-level DPPs in IDTA 02099-1 tooling? Not stated in the pages read.
anomalies: Rule 8: one WebFetch summariser treated the request prompt as an 'embedded instruction' in the GS1 Digital Link page and ignored part of it; no text addressed to an agent was found in any fetched page.

UNTP Identity Resolver (both GitHub archived and GitLab main) links the label ISO/IEC 18975 to https://www.iso.org/standard/83389.html, which search results show is ISO/IEC 18004:2024 (QR code); GitLab main also links 18975 to .../85540.html elsewhere on the same page.

UNTP archived GitHub copy (2025-07-08) used 12-digit GTINs in Digital Link examples (/01/733240226591), contrary to the 14-digit rule since Digital Link 1.4.0; GitLab main (read 2026-10-19) now uses 14-digit examples and makes linkType=all a deprecated alias.
UNTP proposes the identifier form uuid:{UUID}, which is not the RFC 9562 URN form urn:uuid:{UUID}.
UNTP suggests UUIDs as unguessable shared secrets for item data, while RFC 9562 says UUIDs must not be used as security capabilities.
GS1-Conformant Resolver 1.2.1 names no redirect status code, while UNTP IDR specifies 307; GS1 uses /.well-known/gs1resolver and UNTP /.well-known/resolver.
GS1 resolver 1.2.1 returns 404 for an unavailable link type; version 1.1 redirected to the default link, so older resolvers behave differently.
gs1/TDT README targets TDS 2.2 and TDT 2.2 while TDS 2.3 (Oct 2025) is current; the '++' schemes may be missing from the demo artefacts (not checked).
Catena-X CX-0010 3.0.1 page: the structure table lists the prefix as one character, which conflicts with the 16-character total and the text; the older PDF URL for v2.0.0 returned HTTP 404.

CEN catalogue title of EN 18221 ('Data storage, archiving, and data persistence') differs slightly from the Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736 Annex title ('Data storage, archiving, and persistence'); EN 18222 titles also differ in one article. EN 18239 and EN 18246 show date 2026-09-16 in the CEN list.
IDTA 02099-1 cites FprEN 18219:2026 for uniqueProductIdentifier and economicOperatorId but EN 18219:2026 for facilityId, while EN 18219:2026 was published on 2026-05-27.
iso.org returned HTTP 403 for all catalogue pages in this session (prior research on 2026-10-13 could read them); ISO metadata here is secondary_only.
EUR-Lex HTML and PDF endpoints returned empty pages; the Publications Office Cellar manifestations worked.
The AAS antora documentation URLs (admin-shell-io.github.io and industrialdigitaltwin.io/aas-specs-antora/...) returned 301 then 404; the GitHub sources were used instead.
GS1 General Specifications could not be fetched (larger than the 10 MB fetch limit); the mod-10 check-digit algorithm is therefore cited from the engine's existing implementation, not re-read.
The engine's identifier.parse serial set [A-Za-z0-9._-] is narrower than GS1 character set 82 for AI 21, so valid GS1 serials can be rejected (tester false negative).
